nodes.label: Hybrid Data Fetching Strategy
nodes.rationale: Server Components for SEO-critical pages (products, categories) — rendered server-side, no API URL exposure. React Query for client state (cart, session) — caching, optimistic updates, real-time feel.

nodes.label: HTTP-Only Cookie Auth
nodes.source_location: 2.4 Auth: HTTP-Only Cookies via Route Handlers
nodes.rationale: JWT from Strapi stored in HTTP-only cookie (inaccessible to JavaScript). Next.js Route Handlers proxy Strapi auth endpoints. Server Components read cookies for session. Anti-XSS — token not exposed to client JS.

nodes.label: Separate Frontend/Backend Repos
nodes.rationale: Frontend and backend can have own CI/CD. No blocking during development. Clean separation of concerns.

nodes.label: Next.js Breaking Changes Awareness
nodes.rationale: This version of Next.js has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may differ from training data. Must read relevant guide in node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code. Heed deprecation notices.

nodes.label: LLM Coding Behavioral Guidelines
nodes.rationale: Four principles: 1) Think Before Coding — state assumptions, surface tradeoffs. 2) Simplicity First — minimum code, no speculation. 3) Surgical Changes — touch only what you must. 4) Goal-Driven Execution — define success criteria, loop until verified.

nodes.label: middleware.ts to proxy.ts Migration
nodes.rationale: In Next.js 16, middleware.ts is deprecated. If middleware is needed (auth guard, redirect), rename to proxy.ts.
